![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/05003be9090f98f39a65d9ec33e8568fa43ec5c427e34398e4932708f8a03ccc.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=4,$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=4.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ 4 & =\frac{11x-12}{x+4} \\ 4(x+4) & =11x-12 \\ 4x+16 & =11x-12 \\ 7x & =28 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =11x-12=11(4)-12=32, \\ AC & =x+4=4+4=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 32\cdot 8 \\  & =128.\end{aligned}
$$
